text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.
LONDON - Stocks rose for the first time in seven sessions, boosted by strength on Wall Street and speculation about possible takeovers. The FTSE 100 added 19.1 points to 4,576.2.

FRANKFURT - German shares posted minor gains amid relief that the Bundesbank and Bonn seemed close to reconciliation in their spat over asset revaluation. The 30-share DAX rose 11.19 points to 3,673.03, and in after-hours trading stood at 3,684.60.

PARIS - French shares rallied as investors expressed relief at the composition of the Socialist-led government, which included Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn, who is well known to investors, and assigned only one big portfolio, transport, to the Communists. The CAC-40 index closed up 55.48, or 2.11 percent, at 2,690.85.

ZURICH - Swiss shares posted their third consecutive record close, partly on merger and spin-off rumours in the financial sector. The prospect for low interest rates and strength on Wall Street also boosted prices. The broad Swiss Performance Index rose 14.28 points to 3,327.99.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended lower, bruised by profit-taking after three days of gains. The 225-share Nikkei average shed 123.41 points to 20,488.15.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed modestly lower after a day of choppy trading, with the Hang Seng Index off 36.06 points to 14,795.52.
SYDNEY - The Australian stock market ended near its lows after sitting in negative territory all day. The benchmark All Ordinaries Index lost 11.7 points to 2,604.2.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares rallied for the fourth consecutive day on heavy foreign and local buying. The industrial index gained 41.5 points to 8,469.9, the all-share index added 45.7 to 7,218.5 while the gold index lost 5.4 points to 1,140.3.
